ideas.title: We sell AI visibility. AI doesn't know we exist.
ideas.core_idea: Measure your own AI visibility before you market it — our first test found AfriShield cited zero times, and that baseline is the starting line of a public experiment.
ideas.hook: We sell AI visibility. So we tested whether AI knows AfriShield exists. Four regions, eight buyer questions: zero mentions.
ideas.audience: African business owners and marketers evaluating AI SEO agencies
ideas.context: Our 2026-08-30 entity baseline: AfriShield surfaced 0 times across 8 buyer-intent prompts plus a brand search in West, Central, East and North Africa (measured with a web-search proxy).
ideas.problem: Agencies sell visibility they have never measured for themselves.
ideas.insight: Nobody owns the AI answer for AI SEO in Central Africa yet; a baseline of zero is a measurable starting point.
ideas.lesson: Test what AI says about you before you pay anyone — including us.
ideas.visual_concept: Founder on camera, then the real baseline table (regions × prompts, all zeros) as proof; SignalPath showing the missing link between the buyer's question and AfriShield.

real_story.note: Say 'in our first test' — the measurement used a web-search proxy, not per-engine counts.

humor.line: The cobbler's children, now with AI.

new_angle.explanation: No calendar item reports AfriShield's own baseline; it opens a public build-in-public arc.

score_breakdown.rationale: Curiosity/novelty 10: an AI-visibility firm admitting zero citations is unexpected and unpublished. Proof 9: baseline doc exists but per-engine numbers still need a re-run.

ideas.title: 44 of 45 had no website
ideas.core_idea: West African businesses selling seriously on TikTok have no page AI can read; a one-page site is step zero of AI visibility.
ideas.hook: 44 out of 45. That's how many businesses in our TikTok research had no website — and these aren't side hustles.
ideas.audience: real estate agencies and SMB sellers in Cameroon and West Africa who sell through TikTok and WhatsApp
ideas.context: AfriShield lead research, Aug 2026: 45 businesses (real estate, agencies, e-commerce) across Cameroon, Nigeria, Côte d'Ivoire, Senegal and Guinea; 44 had no website; many captions listed two or three phone numbers.
ideas.problem: The storefront is a caption and a WhatsApp number — invisible to anything that reads the web.
ideas.insight: AI assistants answer from pages they can read and verify; a feed caption isn't one.
ideas.lesson: One page with services, prices, location and one routed contact is enough to start.
ideas.visual_concept: Anonymized tracker view (no business names) as ProofFlash → carousel-style Comparison 'caption only vs one-page site' → SignalPath from buyer's question to the seller AI names.

humor.line: The CRM is a WhatsApp thread. The website is a caption.

new_angle.explanation: Original count from our own research; existing 'do you need a website' items have no data.

score_breakdown.rationale: Platform 10: a single striking number carries a carousel, Threads and LinkedIn natively. Story 7: observation, not a narrative with one protagonist.

ideas.title: Who owns page one in African tourism?
ideas.core_idea: In our 5-city pilot, tourism businesses owned far less of their own search results than professional services — aggregators hold the shelf, which is the gap AI visibility work targets.
ideas.hook: In our pilot search study, hotels and safari companies owned about a quarter of their own page one. Accounting and law firms owned about two-thirds.
ideas.audience: hotel, lodge and safari operators in Nairobi, Arusha, Accra, Lagos and Johannesburg
ideas.context: AfriShield's published 9-search, 5-city pilot (Aug 2026): own-site share of page one ~23% for travel/hospitality vs ~68% for professional services; Google showed an AI answer on 9 of 9 queries.
ideas.problem: Tourism businesses rent their shelf space from aggregators and OTAs.
ideas.insight: If aggregators own page one, they are also what AI reads first.
ideas.lesson: Own at least one page that answers the traveler's exact question better than the aggregator does.
ideas.cta: Share this with a hotel owner
ideas.visual_concept: Dashboard of the two shares (with 'pilot · 9 searches · 5 cities' source line) → SearchResult reconstruction labeled ILLUSTRATION → BeforeAfter aggregator-owned vs own-site.

new_angle.explanation: First time the pilot study's numbers appear in social content; calendar tourism items have no original data.

score_breakdown.rationale: Proof 10: published dataset. Story 6: data, not narrative. Curiosity 8: the tourism vs professional services contrast is the hook.

ideas.title: I'm asking ChatGPT for the best hotels in Douala — live
ideas.core_idea: An on-camera test of what AI recommends for Douala hospitality, showing the real result whatever it is, and what the named businesses have that others don't.
ideas.hook: I'm going to ask ChatGPT for the best hotels in Douala. Live. No edits. Let's see who it knows.
ideas.audience: hotel and guesthouse owners in Douala, Kribi and Yaoundé
ideas.context: Cameroon appears in 4 of 195 calendar items although it is the founder's home market and the entity baseline found no GEO incumbent in Central Africa.
ideas.problem: Local hotels don't know whether AI recommends them.
ideas.insight: The businesses AI names usually have readable, consistent information across their own site and listings — to be verified against the real answer on camera.
ideas.lesson: Run the same test for your own business this week; the result is the baseline.
ideas.visual_concept: Founder on camera → unedited screen recording of the query (AIChat frames the real transcript) → CircleHighlight on each name → founder reacts → one pattern explained.

real_story.note: Must be performed on camera; screen recording live, both outcomes scripted.

new_angle.explanation: Existing AI-recommendation tests are Arusha/Nairobi; none run in Douala.

score_breakdown.rationale: Proof 6: created on camera, not yet existing. Novelty 7: format exists in the calendar, new city/market.

ideas.title: My first five business TikToks all died at ~120 views
ideas.core_idea: Product-first openers get scrolled past; a story or stake in the first three seconds is the difference — shown with our own numbers.
ideas.hook: My first five business TikToks all stalled around 120 views. The one story I told got the most comments. Here's the three-second difference.
ideas.audience: small business owners making their own short videos
ideas.context: Our Metricool data and 2026-09-06 hook audit: product-first openers stayed in the ~100–150 view bucket; the story-led White House post drew the most comments.
ideas.problem: Owners open with the product or their title, and nobody stays.
ideas.insight: Viewers stay for tension, not introductions; the product belongs at the end of the story.
ideas.lesson: Rewrite your first sentence as a stake or contradiction; name the product last.
ideas.visual_concept: Dashboard of our six real posts (views/comments) → BeforeAfter of a product-first opener vs a story opener → ProcessFlow: stake, story, product last.

real_story.note: Retention metrics are unavailable — talk about views and comments only.

humor.line: Nobody scrolls TikTok hoping to meet a founder.

new_angle.explanation: Hook advice exists everywhere; our own before/after numbers don't.

score_breakdown.rationale: Business relevance 6: helpful to owners but indirect to AI visibility services. Education 9: immediately applicable.

ideas.title: AI gave me a perfect team list. It was invented.
ideas.core_idea: AI-assisted research can return confident, fabricated names; an AI assistant is only useful if every name it gives you is verified.
ideas.hook: I used AI to research a company's leadership team before reaching out. The list looked perfect. It was invented.
ideas.audience: consultants, accountants and lawyers using AI assistants for prospect research
ideas.context: During our Sept 2026 market research, one scraped 'team list' was fabricated and was caught during verification against public records.
ideas.problem: Emailing a person who doesn't exist burns credibility and domain reputation.
ideas.insight: AI is good at structure and bad at admitting it doesn't know; verification is part of the task, not an extra.
ideas.lesson: Before you use a name AI gave you, find that person on a second, independent source.
ideas.visual_concept: StoryCard (company unnamed) → Warning 'unverified names' → ProcessFlow: generate, verify on 2 sources, then use.

real_story.note: Never name the company whose list was fabricated.

new_angle.explanation: Calendar AI FAILS items are about AI misunderstanding businesses; none about AI research fabricating people.

score_breakdown.rationale: Proof 7: our own record exists but can't be shown (company anonymized). CTA 6: lesson post, weak lead ask.

ideas.title: One bar of signal: does your booking page survive?
ideas.core_idea: A real mobile test of hotel booking pages under weak signal shows whether a guest can actually book — speed is part of being chosen.
ideas.hook: Five hotel booking pages. One bar of signal. A stopwatch. Let's see which ones a guest could actually book.
ideas.audience: hotel and lodge owners in Cameroon and Tanzania whose guests book on mobile
ideas.context: The One Bar Test series is defined in the operating system but was never scheduled; guests in our markets often browse on weak mobile connections.
ideas.problem: A beautiful site that doesn't load on one bar loses the booking silently.
ideas.insight: Throttled-network loading exposes heavy images and scripts that office Wi-Fi hides.
ideas.lesson: Test your own booking page on a throttled connection and remove the heaviest element first.
ideas.visual_concept: Split-screen phone recordings with timers (real, throttled network, same device) → MetricCounter per page → Success/Warning results; pages shown with owners' consent or anonymized.

real_story.note: Performed on camera; anonymize the sites unless owners volunteer.

humor.line: The guest is still waiting. So is the booking.

new_angle.explanation: Activates an unused series with a measurable test.

score_breakdown.rationale: Proof 6: must be filmed. Relevance 7: page speed is adjacent to AI visibility, strongest for CONVERTED.

ideas.title: What a law firm's website must say for AI to recommend it
ideas.core_idea: Professional services already own their search results more than tourism does; the question is whether their pages answer the client's real question in words AI can quote.
ideas.hook: In our pilot, professional firms owned about two-thirds of their own search results. Owning the page isn't the same as answering the question.
ideas.audience: managing partners of law and accounting firms in Nairobi, Lagos and Douala
ideas.context: Professional services is 6pp under target in the calendar; our pilot shows they already own their page one, so the next step is quotable answers.
ideas.problem: Firm websites describe the firm, not the client's problem.
ideas.insight: AI quotes pages that state a specific service, jurisdiction and process in plain sentences.
ideas.lesson: Add one page per core service that answers who it's for, where, what happens and what it costs to start.
ideas.visual_concept: LinkedIn document carousel: pilot data slide with source → 5-part page framework → before/after sentence rewrite labeled illustration.

new_angle.explanation: Professional-services angle on the pilot data (the tourism idea uses the other half).

score_breakdown.rationale: Curiosity/novelty 6: the framework itself is familiar; the pilot number is the only new element. Keep in the bank unless reframed.

matches.hook: In our pilot search study, hotels and safari companies owned about a quarter of their own page one. Accounting and law firms owned about two-thirds.

ideas.title: How I built a WhatsApp assistant that speaks Pidgin
ideas.core_idea: A non-developer can assemble a trilingual WhatsApp assistant from affordable tools; the carousel shows the actual stack and the order to build it.
ideas.hook: I built a WhatsApp assistant that replies in French, English and Pidgin — and I'm not a developer. Here's the exact stack.
ideas.audience: salon and clinic owners in Cameroon who take bookings on WhatsApp
ideas.context: Ben's Eva build (Sep 2026) using Supabase, the WhatsApp API, Claude and Fapshi; the Sep 9 TikTok announced it.
ideas.problem: Bookings and questions pile up in WhatsApp after hours.
ideas.insight: The pieces exist and are affordable; the hard part is the order and the guardrails.
ideas.lesson: Start with FAQs and booking requests only; add payments last.
ideas.visual_concept: Instagram carousel: stack diagram as SignalPath (WhatsApp → assistant → calendar → payment) → one slide per build step → guardrails slide.

real_story.note: Do NOT claim 'booking real salon clients' or the $20,000 quote — both unverified.

new_angle.explanation: The Sep 9 post announced Eva; this is the step-by-step build carousel it never showed.

score_breakdown.rationale: Novelty 7: already announced publicly; the tutorial angle is new.

matches.hook: I built an AI receptionist with zero coding experience — and she's booking real salon clients right now 👇 Meet Eva: an AI WhatsApp assistant for small businesses that replies 24/7 in French, English & Pidgin, books appo

ideas.title: My content calendar had better stories than my business
ideas.core_idea: Auditing a content plan against reality shows where it invents convenient stories; receipts beat ideas.
ideas.hook: I audited my own 180-day content calendar. 25 posts described things I couldn't prove happened.
ideas.audience: founders and marketers planning content with AI tools
ideas.context: The Content Autopilot's first gap analysis (2026-09-14) flagged 25 calendar rows that narrate events with no evidence, 29 past-due days, and Cameroon in 4 of 195 items.
ideas.problem: Plans written in one sitting — especially with AI — fill gaps with plausible stories.
ideas.insight: A plan needs an evidence column; every 'a client told me' needs a receipt or a rewrite.
ideas.lesson: Before adding more ideas, check the plan against what actually happened.
ideas.visual_concept: Founder at desk → real gap report on screen (ProofFlash + Screenshot) → Warning on the flagged count → ProcessFlow: link a receipt, film it, or label it hypothetical.

real_story.note: Say 'couldn't prove', not 'never happened' — some may be real but undocumented.

humor.line: My calendar had a better imagination than my business.

new_angle.explanation: Build-in-public moment from this week; nothing like it in the calendar.

score_breakdown.rationale: Relevance 5 and CTA 5: speaks to marketers more than to hotel owners. Strong LinkedIn/Threads trust piece, weak lead driver.
